heading: The inflation rate in the United States
cell_title: Website version: Fig. 1 with buttons for the two views and the G20 economies in the legend
plot_title: United States: inflation peaked at 13.5% in 1980; 2025: 2.6%
source_note:
**Sources.** Data: [U.S. Bureau of Labor Statistics, Consumer Price Index for All Urban Consumers (`CPIAUCSL`), via FRED](https://fred.stlouisfed.org/series/CPIAUCSL), annual averages, for the United States;
[World Bank, World Development Indicators, Inflation, consumer prices (`FP.CPI.TOTL.ZG`)](https://data.worldbank.org/indicator/FP.CPI.TOTL.ZG) for the other economies, with gaps filled from the [World Bank's Global Inflation Database](https://www.worldbank.org/en/research/brief/inflation-database) (Ha, Kose and Ohnsorge 2023).
Prepared files: [`data/ch08/fig8-1.csv`](https://github.com/quarcs-lab/macro102-site/blob/main/data/ch08/fig8-1.csv), [`data/ch08/inflation_panel.csv`](https://github.com/quarcs-lab/macro102-site/blob/main/data/ch08/inflation_panel.csv) and [`data/ch08/countries.csv`](https://github.com/quarcs-lab/macro102-site/blob/main/data/ch08/countries.csv)
(see the [data notes](https://github.com/quarcs-lab/macro102-site/blob/main/data/ch08/README.md)).
Chart: inspired by Fig. 8.1 in Jones (2024), [*Macroeconomics*, 6th ed.](https://wwnorton.com/books/9781324063612)

heading: The percentage of countries experiencing high inflation

heading: Money growth and inflation in the United States
cell_title: Website version: Fig. 3 with a precomputed slider for the length of the periods and 17 more countries
plot_title: 10-year periods: correlation 0.76, average gap g_M − π = 4.0 points
source_note:
**Sources.** Data: [Jordà–Schularick–Taylor Macrohistory Database, release 6, broad money (`money`) and the CPI (`cpi`)](https://www.macrohistory.net/database/)
(Jordà, Schularick and Taylor 2017), 18 economies, 1870–2020; for the United States since 1959,
[Board of Governors of the Federal Reserve System, M2 (`M2NS`), via FRED](https://fred.stlouisfed.org/series/M2NS),
and [MeasuringWorth, Officer and Williamson, The Annual Consumer Price Index for the United States, 1774–Present](https://www.measuringworth.com/datasets/uscpi/).
Prepared files: [`data/ch08/fig8-3.csv`](https://github.com/quarcs-lab/macro102-site/blob/main/data/ch08/fig8-3.csv) and [`data/ch08/money_prices_panel.csv`](https://github.com/quarcs-lab/macro102-site/blob/main/data/ch08/money_prices_panel.csv) (see the [data notes](https://github.com/quarcs-lab/macro102-site/blob/main/data/ch08/README.md)).
Chart: inspired by Fig. 8.3 in Jones (2024), [*Macroeconomics*, 6th ed.](https://wwnorton.com/books/9781324063612)

heading: Money growth and inflation in the United States
plot_title: M2 velocity stayed near 1.8 until about 1990, then rose and fell
source_note:
**Sources.** Data: [U.S. Bureau of Economic Analysis, Gross Domestic Product (`GDPA`), via FRED](https://fred.stlouisfed.org/series/GDPA);
[Board of Governors of the Federal Reserve System, M2 (`M2SL`), via FRED](https://fred.stlouisfed.org/series/M2SL), calendar-year averages.
Prepared file: [`data/ch08/us_money_annual.csv`](https://github.com/quarcs-lab/macro102-site/blob/main/data/ch08/us_money_annual.csv) (see the [data notes](https://github.com/quarcs-lab/macro102-site/blob/main/data/ch08/README.md)).
Chart: inspired by the discussion of velocity in Chapter 8 of Jones (2024), [*Macroeconomics*, 6th ed.](https://wwnorton.com/books/9781324063612), which has no figure of it.

heading: Real and nominal interest rates in the United States
cell_title: Website version: Fig. 5 with a menu of 50 countries
plot_title: United States: the real rate R = i − π was negative in 23 of 66 years
source_note:
**Sources.** Data: for the United States,
[Board of Governors of the Federal Reserve System, 3-Month Treasury Bill Secondary Market Rate (`TB3MS`), via FRED](https://fred.stlouisfed.org/series/TB3MS)
and [U.S. Bureau of Labor Statistics, Consumer Price Index for All Urban Consumers (`CPIAUCSL`), via FRED](https://fred.stlouisfed.org/series/CPIAUCSL); for the other economies, the 3-month interest rate from the
[OECD Data Explorer](https://data-explorer.oecd.org/): Economic Outlook No. 119, short-term interest rate (`IRS`,
dataflow `DSD_EO@DF_EO`), with earlier years from the OECD's financial-market statistics, 3-month interbank rate
(`IR3TIB`, dataflow `DSD_STES@DF_FINMARK`; also on FRED, e.g. [Germany, `IR3TIB01DEM156N`](https://fred.stlouisfed.org/series/IR3TIB01DEM156N)),
and inflation from [World Bank, World Development Indicators, Inflation, consumer prices (`FP.CPI.TOTL.ZG`)](https://data.worldbank.org/indicator/FP.CPI.TOTL.ZG) and the [World Bank's Global Inflation Database](https://www.worldbank.org/en/research/brief/inflation-database) (Ha, Kose and Ohnsorge 2023).
Prepared files: [`data/ch08/fig8-5.csv`](https://github.com/quarcs-lab/macro102-site/blob/main/data/ch08/fig8-5.csv) and [`data/ch08/interest_rates_panel.csv`](https://github.com/quarcs-lab/macro102-site/blob/main/data/ch08/interest_rates_panel.csv) (see the [data notes](https://github.com/quarcs-lab/macro102-site/blob/main/data/ch08/README.md)).
Chart: inspired by Fig. 8.5 in Jones (2024), [*Macroeconomics*, 6th ed.](https://wwnorton.com/books/9781324063612)

heading: Hyperinflations in Argentina, Brazil, and Russia
cell_title: Website version: Fig. 6 with buttons for the vertical scale and the 31 hyperinflations in the legend
source_note:
**Sources.** Data: World Bank, World Development Indicators, Inflation, consumer prices, via FRED:
[Argentina (`FPCPITOTLZGARG`)](https://fred.stlouisfed.org/series/FPCPITOTLZGARG),
[Brazil (`FPCPITOTLZGBRA`)](https://fred.stlouisfed.org/series/FPCPITOTLZGBRA) and
[Russia (`FPCPITOTLZGRUS`)](https://fred.stlouisfed.org/series/FPCPITOTLZGRUS); Argentina before 2018 from the [World Bank's Global Inflation Database](https://www.worldbank.org/en/research/brief/inflation-database) (Ha, Kose and Ohnsorge 2023);
the other economies from [World Bank, World Development Indicators, Inflation, consumer prices (`FP.CPI.TOTL.ZG`)](https://data.worldbank.org/indicator/FP.CPI.TOTL.ZG) and the Global Inflation Database.
Prepared files: [`data/ch08/fig8-6.csv`](https://github.com/quarcs-lab/macro102-site/blob/main/data/ch08/fig8-6.csv), [`data/ch08/fig8-7.csv`](https://github.com/quarcs-lab/macro102-site/blob/main/data/ch08/fig8-7.csv) and [`data/ch08/inflation_panel.csv`](https://github.com/quarcs-lab/macro102-site/blob/main/data/ch08/inflation_panel.csv) (see the [data notes](https://github.com/quarcs-lab/macro102-site/blob/main/data/ch08/README.md)).
Chart: inspired by Fig. 8.6 in Jones (2024), [*Macroeconomics*, 6th ed.](https://wwnorton.com/books/9781324063612)

heading: High inflation in Mexico, Nigeria, and Venezuela
plot_title: 22 economies peaked between 100% and 500%: high inflation, no hyperinflation
source_note:
**Sources.** Data: World Bank, World Development Indicators, Inflation, consumer prices, via FRED:
[Mexico (`FPCPITOTLZGMEX`)](https://fred.stlouisfed.org/series/FPCPITOTLZGMEX),
[Nigeria (`FPCPITOTLZGNGA`)](https://fred.stlouisfed.org/series/FPCPITOTLZGNGA) and
[Venezuela (`FPCPITOTLZGVEN`)](https://fred.stlouisfed.org/series/FPCPITOTLZGVEN); Venezuela after 2016 from the [World Bank's Global Inflation Database](https://www.worldbank.org/en/research/brief/inflation-database) (Ha, Kose and Ohnsorge 2023);
the other economies, and the bar chart of peaks, from [World Bank, World Development Indicators, Inflation, consumer prices (`FP.CPI.TOTL.ZG`)](https://data.worldbank.org/indicator/FP.CPI.TOTL.ZG) and the Global Inflation Database (Zimbabwe 2001–2008 dropped).
Prepared files: [`data/ch08/fig8-7.csv`](https://github.com/quarcs-lab/macro102-site/blob/main/data/ch08/fig8-7.csv), [`data/ch08/fig8-6.csv`](https://github.com/quarcs-lab/macro102-site/blob/main/data/ch08/fig8-6.csv) and [`data/ch08/inflation_panel.csv`](https://github.com/quarcs-lab/macro102-site/blob/main/data/ch08/inflation_panel.csv) (see the [data notes](https://github.com/quarcs-lab/macro102-site/blob/main/data/ch08/README.md)).
